chapter: The district underworld and street musicians
title: Rabbit Brown and the 'Spoonful' guitarist who hustled alone
summary: Dawson recalls Rabbit Brown hustling without a band, and a guitar player singing Spoonful in barbershops and the French Market for tips.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Where the blues came from: Handy, Bolden and early blues

blocks.x: Did you know that song about the downfall of the lion? You remember Rabbit Brown used to be?
Rabbit Brown, yeah, I know. Rabbit Brown, yeah. Oh, you knew him? Yeah, did I know him? Yes, indeed, I know him. A little old Rabbit Brown.
Where did he used to be?
He used to, let's see what Rabbit was playing. Get tough.

Nowhere. Just hustling, yeah. Just like old, they had a fellow that called, what's his name? Oh, he was a hustler. Guitar player. Used to sing Spoonful. I've been so long, it takes me time to think, you know. I can't think of that man's name. He lived right across from the school on Saturday, Turbo Street.
Did he play with bands at all?

No. He just played by himself. He was stuck, grabbed the brownie? He just hustled, yeah. He could take the guitar and go out by himself and come back and hustle and make more money than what you do, make a playing music.
And he sang about a spoonful?

Yeah, he used to sing that song by the spoonful, All I Want Was a Spoonful. Yeah. He just hit the head on the guitar, sing that song, you know. He'd go all over, go way down by the French Market, all down to Buccarat.

And that's all he'd do. He'd hit the guitar, go to the barbershop, and the barbershop would crowd with people. Hit the guitar there, what'd you say there, people? Oh, all right, he'd start the singing and pass the hat around in the barbershop.
